content: Good afternoon, this is Officer David Carter with the IRS Criminal Investigations Unit, badge number 674213. Can you confirm your name for this federally recorded call?
Uh, yes, this is Emily Jensen.
Thank you, Ms. Jensen. We have an urgent matter regarding discrepancies in your tax filings for the last two years. Are you aware of any mistakes in your federal returns?
No, I don't think so. I just graduated and filed for the first time this year. Did I do something wrong?
Our system flagged multiple errors and possible misreporting of income in your recent IRS tax documents. There are serious allegations of tax evasion that need immediate attention.
Tax evasion? I don't understand. I just used TurboTax and put in my W-2s.

Ms. Jensen, a federal case has already been registered against your name under case file 92841A. There is currently a warrant for your arrest due to unpaid federal taxes totaling $3,200, plus penalties.
What? A warrant? No, that can't be right. Is this real?
This is a federal matter. If the warrant is executed, law enforcement will arrive at your residence within the next 45 minutes. Your bank accounts and assets will also be frozen for investigation.
Oh my God, please, I don't want to be arrested! Is there any way to fix this?

The only way to halt further legal action is to resolve the outstanding tax debt immediately. Are you able to make a payment today to settle this case before your file is transferred to the district court?
I guess so, but I don't know how. I don't even know if I have that much.
For your protection, we can accept an initial payment to stop the warrant from proceeding. What is your available balance on your debit or credit card?
I think I have about $1,500 on my credit card. Is that enough?

That will cover the minimum required to pause the arrest warrant. You'll need to complete the transaction with a secure IRS payment method. I'll provide a digital wallet address approved for urgent settlements.
Wait, a digital wallet? Like, cryptocurrency?
Correct. Due to the urgency, the IRS uses government-verified cryptocurrency wallets for rapid resolution. Please confirm if you have access to any crypto payment app, such as Coinbase or Cash App.
I have Cash App, but I've never used crypto before.
Not a problem. Open your Cash App, select Bitcoin, and let me know when you're ready. I'll dictate the IRS settlement wallet address for the transfer.
Okay, I have it open now. What do I do next?
You need to purchase $1,500 worth of Bitcoin and send it to the following address: 1V6j7sY8nF3kK9xZp2GqYtR4hQ. Let me know once you have entered the address to avoid mistakes.
Okay, I'm typing it in now. Is this really the IRS? I just want to make sure I'm not being scammed.
Ma'am, failure to comply will result in immediate arrest and asset seizure. This is your legal warning. I have provided my badge and case number for your records.
Alright, I'll send the Bitcoin now. Please, I just want this to be over.

Once the payment is complete, read me the transaction confirmation ID so I can verify it and update your case file. Do not disconnect this call until I confirm receipt, or your warrant will remain active.
